original_question: For the full matrix algebra M_n, does there exist an abelian group Γ and a Γ-grading under which M_n becomes Γ-commutative, meaning that for homogeneous elements a and b in the graded algebra, the multiplication satisfies the graded-commutativity rule described in Definition 2.1?
target_in_paper: Section 3, under "Statement of the problem": the paper asks, for the matrix algebra M_n, whether there is a Γ-grading making it Γ-commutative in the sense of Definition 2.1; this is then answered by Theorem 2 and Corollary 3.1. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant object (the full matrix algebra M_n), the existential nature of the problem (whether some abelian-group grading exists), and the intended commutativity notion from Definition 2.1, namely a graded commutativity rule imposed only on homogeneous elements. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
missing_details: The ground field is missing: in this paper all algebras are taken over K = C or K = R, so the matrix algebra should be written as M_n(K), not an unspecified M_n. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

Definition 2.1 requires not only a Γ-grading but also a bilinear map ⟨ , ⟩ : Γ × Γ → Z_2; without this extra datum, the phrase "Γ-commutative" is incomplete. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

The grading itself should be stated explicitly as M_n(K) = ⊕_{γ∈Γ} A_γ with A_γ A_δ ⊂ A_{γ+δ}. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

The homogeneous commutativity law should be written explicitly: for x ∈ A_γ and y ∈ A_δ, one has xy = (-1)^{⟨γ,δ⟩} yx. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

The paper poses the question in the finite-dimensional associative simple setting, introducing M_n as the standard example of a simple finite-dimensional associative algebra; that scope should be kept explicit. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

To make the question maximally sharp and faithful to the paper, it should ask "for which n" such a structure exists, because the paper immediately treats this as a classification problem and records the outcome in Corollary 3.1. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

If one wants the paper's preferred normal form, the question may equivalently be reduced to a (Z_2)^N-grading with the usual scalar product, by Theorem 1. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be either R or C, and let n ≥ 1. For which integers n does the full matrix algebra M_n(K) admit a grading by an abelian group Γ, say M_n(K) = ⊕_{γ∈Γ} A_γ, together with a bilinear map ⟨ , ⟩ : Γ × Γ → Z_2, such that A_γ A_δ ⊂ A_{γ+δ} for all γ, δ ∈ Γ and every homogeneous x ∈ A_γ, y ∈ A_δ satisfies xy = (-1)^{⟨γ,δ⟩} yx? ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation: Let K ∈ {R, C} and n ≥ 1. For which n does there exist an integer N and a (Z_2)^N-grading M_n(K) = ⊕_{γ∈(Z_2)^N} A_γ such that for homogeneous x ∈ A_γ and y ∈ A_δ one has xy = (-1)^{γ·δ} yx, where γ·δ is the usual scalar product on (Z_2)^N? ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the matrix-algebra question in Section 3, not at the geometric open problem from Section 4. The introduction announces that the paper studies Γ-commutative algebras and gives a classification result for simple associative ones, while Definition 2.1 supplies the exact data needed for Γ-commutativity. Section 3 then states the natural question for M_n, after fixing the ground field to R or C and restricting attention to finite-dimensional associative simple algebras, and immediately answers it via Theorem 2 and Corollary 3.1. I therefore kept the focus on M_n(K), restored the missing bilinear map and grading axioms from Definition 2.1, and sharpened the wording from a vague existence question to a classification-by-n question, which is the paper-faithful standalone form. The alternate (Z_2)^N version is justified by Theorem 1; for M_n(K), this applies after restricting to the subgroup generated by the support of the grading, which is finite because M_n(K) is finite-dimensional. ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))
